title: National Preparedness Month: How to Build a Home Security Plan
summary: September is National Preparedness Month. Here's how to build a home security plan that actually works.
body_markdown:
Emergencies come in all shapes and sizes, and a home security system can help you react to many of them.


It starts with your security cameras. A good camera doesn’t just provide visual coverage of your property; it can capture audio, provide nighttime coverage, shine spotlights to deter invaders, and even send alerts directly to your phone.


Security cameras like the[Arlo Pro 6th Gen](https://us.arlo.com/products/arlo-pro-6) can even lean on machine learning and artificial intelligence to smartly detect specific noises or events like fires and gunshots through its Early Warning System, giving you more specific information that you can respond to more effectively.


Whatever camera you choose, there are a few features you should keep in mind when building out a security system that aligns with your home security plan:


- **Video quality.** 2K video resolution offers fantastic image clarity without taking up too much space or bandwidth, making it especially helpful for detecting suspicious people or objects that enter the frame.
- **Audio capabilities.** A built-in microphone can pick up nearby sounds, like breaking glass or dog barks, notifying you when something happens off screen. Meanwhile, a speaker can work in tandem with the microphone to provide two-way audio, giving you a chance to direct package deliveries or ward off intruders.
- **24/7 monitoring.** Long battery life will allow your cameras to last for months at a time, giving you ‘round-the-clock protection. Meanwhile, services like Arlo Secure integrate with your home security system to provide 24/7 Professional Monitoring, keeping your property secure even if you’re not on the premises.
- **Notifications and alerts.** When your home security system detects something, it should notify you through your smartphone. Getting alerts for fires, noises, or other security events will arm you with the information you need to begin enacting your home security plan.
- **Smart home security integration.** Check if the home security system you’re researching integrates with your existing smart home setup. If it does, you can get all the benefits and features of your new security system and access them within an ecosystem you’re already comfortable with.
